rationale: Interpret receipt fd88bc508e4f413393838b7d64657137, the thirty-second observation of the blocked replay. The 128-batch control returns in 5 ms while the 129-batch case has still not returned after 30 s, which turns the permanence claim from a source-level inference supported by five-second cutoffs into a measurement whose margin over a completed replay is about four orders of magnitude. The account keeps its conclusion and defect claim, extends the rationale with the receipt, rewrites the counterevidence entry that said permanence rested only on timeouts and source reading, and adds a limitation recording that thirty seconds is still finite.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft() calls restoreFromCommittedLogs() synchronously, which clamps the store's staged commit index to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs flushes a commitTuple batch to r.fsmMutateCh every MaxAppendEntries entries and once more for the remainder, and the only goroutine that reads fsmMutateCh (runFSM) is started after NewRaft returns.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; no snapshot restored at or above the staged commit index.

knowledge.statement: For the captured code, the startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches because fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 and its send in processLogs selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; with DefaultConfig MaxAppendEntries=64 this allows at most 8192 committed entries beyond the last snapshot, so 8193 or more replayed entries have no enabled progress path (no consumer exists and shutdownCh has no closer outside a *Raft that NewRaft never returns).
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true, restart with staged commit index exceeding the last snapshot index by more than 128*MaxAppendEntries.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft does not complete a legal replay of already-committed log entries once the replay needs more than 128 FSM dispatch batches; the caller never receives the *Raft, so the node has no way to start, serve or shut down. This is a startup progress failure, not a decision-safety failure: no commit, vote or membership decision was observed to be wrong. Evidence. Receipt d61420dbc49a4072937b040aac55a51c (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): parsed index 1, seeded commit-tracking store with 8192 committed entries = exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=64, returned=true in 5 ms; parsed index 3, the retained state of a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the leader/commit/apply path and then snapshotted at index 8302 above the staged commit index, replay 0 batches, returned=true in 0 ms; parsed index 5, the same seeded store with 8193 entries = 129 batches, returned=false after 5000 ms with one newly blocked (*Raft).processLogs goroutine and one newly blocked (*Raft).restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutine; parsed index 7, the same real-cluster prefix without a snapshot, staged commit 8300 = 130 batches, returned=false after 5000 ms with the same two newly blocked goroutines. Successor receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a (completed, tests_passed, exit 0) reproduced all four outcomes (parsed indices 1, 3, 7, 9) and added parsed index 5: the identical 8193-entry store state that hangs at MaxAppendEntries=64, replayed as 9 batches with MaxAppendEntries=1024, returned=true in 2 ms. That comparison holds entry count, log content, staged commit index and snapshot state fixed and varies only the batch size, so the stall is attributable to the number of batches relative to the 128-slot channel rather than to log volume, snapshot handling, store state or the producing cluster; the goroutine match in both hanging cases localizes the block to processLogs invoked from restoreFromCommittedLogs. Mechanism from source: api.go:606 calls restoreFromCommittedLogs before any background goroutine exists; api.go:753 calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); raft.go:1303-1313 sends each commitTuple batch into fsmMutateCh and selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 (api.go:560); its only reader runFSM (fsm.go:241) is started at api.go:637 after NewRaft returns; api.go:1065 is the only closer of shutdownCh and is reachable only through a *Raft. After 128 successful sends the 129th send therefore has no producer and no possible closer, so the block is permanent rather than slow. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a node restarting with the documented RestoreCommittedLogs option and with more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond its last snapshot hangs inside NewRaft indefinitely while reporting no error. The operational restart path was measured separately in receipt f032fc49841048c9877653db9f877b27: a three-voter cluster committed 8400 commands, one follower accumulated them and staged its own commit index at 8400 with last log index 8402, and only that follower was restarted. With a snapshot taken on that follower at 8400 the replay was 0 batches and NewRaft returned in 0 ms (parsed index 1, comparison holds); without the snapshot the same follower needed 132 batches and NewRaft had not returned after 5000 ms (parsed index 3, comparison violated). The boundary therefore reproduces from the follower's own appendEntries-driven commit staging, not only from a feeding leader. The boundary was then checked at a second batch size: receipt f8b98d790cc14664af8af17775d3cc48 replays 131072 committed entries at MaxAppendEntries=1024, which is exactly 128 batches, and NewRaft returned in 45 ms (parsed index 7, comparison holds), while 131073 entries, one entry further and therefore 129 batches, did not return within 5000 ms (parsed index 9, comparison violated). The same capacity limit therefore governs a replay whose entry count is sixteen times larger, so the boundary follows the batch count rather than the default entry count. A third configuration point, receipt 14286fc183ac4bbc92a41f73a49a57d9 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0), moves the batch size to its smallest legal value: with MaxAppendEntries=1 the same product predicts a boundary of 128 entries. Parsed index 0 records replay_entries=128, replay_batches=128 and staged_commit_index=128; parsed index 1 records returned=true in 1 ms. Parsed index 2 records replay_entries=129 and replay_batches=129; parsed index 3 records returned=false after 5004 ms with the error 'no return within observation window', fsm_applied_sampled=0 and one new goroutine inside processLogs. The stated product 128*MaxAppendEntries therefore holds at 1, 64 and 1024, a span of 1024 in the entry count at which the block appears, and the smallest case shows the block needs no large volume of data, only one batch more than the channel can hold. A real-prefix case inside the shortened-replay region, receipt 7ee579ae94bd4812beaa21ce1ca9bb2e (completed, tests_passed, exit 0), commits 200 commands, takes a snapshot, commits a second batch and shuts down, so the restart replays only the tail after the snapshot. Parsed index 0 records snapshot_index=202, staged_commit_index=400, last_log_index=402, replay_entries=198 and replay_batches=4; parsed index 1 records returned=true in 3 ms. Parsed index 2 records the same first batch and snapshot with a second batch of 8300, giving staged_commit_index=8501, last_log_index=8502, replay_entries=8299 and replay_batches=130; parsed index 3 records returned=false after 5000 ms with one new goroutine inside processLogs. The recovery region between a zero-length replay and the blocked case is therefore observed on real prefixes rather than inferred: when the snapshot leaves four batches the constructor returns, and when it leaves 130 it does not. Permanence, receipt fd88bc508e4f413393838b7d64657137 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the seeded boundary pair at the default batch size, watched for longer than any earlier receipt. Parsed index 0 records 8192 entries and replay_batches=128 with a ten-second window; parsed index 1 records returned=true in 5 ms. Parsed index 2 records 8193 entries and replay_batches=129 with a thirty-second window; parsed index 3 records returned=false after 30000 ms with one new goroutine inside processLogs. The blocked case therefore outlasts the control's completion by roughly five thousand times, which is evidence of a permanent stall rather than a slow replay, and the source-level argument about the absent consumer and the unreachable closer is no longer the only ground for that claim.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft calls restoreFromCommittedLogs synchronously and processLogs flushes batches into fsmMutateCh while runFSM starts only after NewRaft returns.
The startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches, so 128*MaxAppendEntries replayed entries is the boundary beyond which no progress path exists.

counterevidence: RestoreCommittedLogs is not part of DefaultConfig (config.go:329-341 leaves it false), and with the option disabled restoreFromCommittedLogs returns immediately (api.go:725-727), so default-configured nodes cannot reach the blocked path.

A snapshot at or near the commit index removes the replay entirely: parsed index 3 in receipt d61420dbc49a4072937b040aac55a51c and the short case of receipt 7ee579ae94bd4812beaa21ce1ca9bb2e restarted real prefixes with a small enough tail that NewRaft returned, so snapshot cadence bounds exposure to this path.

A larger MaxAppendEntries moves the boundary: parsed index 5 of receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a completed the very state that hangs at the default batch size, so a deployment that raises MaxAppendEntries enough for 128*MaxAppendEntries to cover its snapshot lag does not encounter the block.

The trigger observations are bounded windows, now including a thirty-second one in receipt fd88bc508e4f413393838b7d64657137, but still finite runs; permanence is claimed from the source-level absence of any consumer before NewRaft returns, from shutdownCh having no closer outside Shutdown on the returned *Raft, and from the blocked case outlasting the 128-batch control's five-millisecond completion by four orders of magnitude.
No incorrect commit, applied entry, vote or membership decision was observed in any case; the evidence contradicts only startup progress.
limitations: The boundary is 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond the last snapshot, and it was exercised at three batch sizes: at 1 the boundary is 128 entries (129 blocked, 128 returned), at 64 it is 8192 entries (8193 blocked, 8192 returned) and at 1024 it is 131072 entries (131073 blocked, 131072 returned). Only three points were sampled, all with one entry per batch unit or a whole multiple of it, and the 128-slot fsmMutateCh capacity is not configurable, so no case varied it.

The seeded cases supply the commit-tracking store state directly. Five restarts rest on a real prefix: a single-node leader (staged commit 8300, last log 8302, because the leader stages the pre-dispatch commit index), a three-voter cluster follower in both the snapshot and no-snapshot cases (staged commit 8400, last log 8402), and the mid-run-snapshot prefixes at staged commits 400 and 8501 over a snapshot at 202.

The shortened-replay region is now measured on real prefixes at four and 130 batches, but no real prefix was restarted with a tail between five and 129 batches; the seeded nine-batch case covers that middle range, and the real-prefix evidence brackets it at both ends rather than sampling inside it.

fsm_applied_sampled is one sample at the end of each window and was 0 in every case, including the returning controls where runFSM had not yet applied anything, so it is not used as evidence of completion.

Out of scope here: whether the installSnapshot and restoreUserSnapshot sends to the same channel can block indefinitely on a running node, where runFSM is already active and would provide backpressure rather than a permanent block.

The longest observation is thirty seconds. A replay that would eventually complete after that remains indistinguishable from one that never completes, although the control of the same shape finishes in milliseconds and the goroutine remains parked in processLogs throughout.
